abstract: Cancer-associated retinopathy (CAR) is a rare cause of vision loss that was first reported in 1976. It is reported that the retinopathy associated with cancer occurs due to antibodies against the tumor antigens that cross-react with retinal cell layers. We present the case of a young male who came to the emergency department with sudden onset of bilateral vision loss. He had a large-sized testicular seminoma with metastatic retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy. Several primary ophthalmological and systemic conditions were considered. He had multiple, positive anti-retinal antibodies. The cancer was felt to be the cause of the vision loss based on the clinical presentation and the presence of anti-retinal antibodies. He was treated with intravenous steroids, plasmapheresis, and curative chemotherapy, but there was no improvement in vision. Unfortunately, he died due to multiorgan failure. Our case is the second on seminoma-associated retinopathy in the literature.
abstract_ja: 癌関連網膜症(CAR)は、1976年に初めて報告された稀な視力障害の原因である。癌に伴う網膜症は、腫瘍抗原に対する抗体が網膜細胞層と交差反応することによって生じると報告されている。突然の両側性視力低下を主訴に救急外来を受診した若年男性の症例を提示する。彼は巨大な精巣セミノーマと転移性後腹膜リンパ節腫大を有していた。原発性の眼科的疾患および全身性疾患が複数考慮された。複数の陽性の抗網膜抗体が認められた。臨床経過および抗網膜抗体の存在から、癌が視力障害の原因と考えられた。静脈内ステロイド、血漿交換および根治的化学療法で治療したが、視力の改善は認められなかった。残念ながら、患者は多臓器不全で死亡した。本症例は、文献上セミノーマ関連網膜症の2例目である。
